# `bin/run-external`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/run-external`](../../../bin/run-external)

## What it says about itself

```text
Launch one worker as a headless MAIN process (not a subagent) on one of three routes: --via openrouter (the default),
--via anthropic (the user's Claude Code login; `claude -p`) or --via codex (the user's Codex login). A new
instance enables anthropic and codex (bin/new-workspace), so name --via on every launch.
LESSONS.md "Every worker is a headless main process" (user, 2026-09-16 09:44 MST): workers launch this way so no harness subagent
note reaches them, and model / effort / tools / turn cap are set per worker on the command line.

  bin/run-external RUN --model ID [--via openrouter|anthropic|codex] [--effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max]
                       [--max-turns N] [--prompt "text"] [--retries N]
                       [--network] [--module NAME ...] [--wall-hours H] [--dry-run] [--detach]
  Refuses (exit 3) without a valid user approval of the run's bytes: bin/approve (LESSONS.md "Every launch and every ledger append consumes a byte-bound").
  LESSONS.md "Networked and Codex launches need their flags bound" (2026-09-22):
  --via codex   the user's Codex login (ChatGPT plan); ID e.g. gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-6-astra. The whole codex
                process runs inside bwrap (bin/_ext.py codex). Codex has no turn cap of its own: --max-turns caps
                its tool calls, counted from the transcript as it arrives (LESSONS.md "A Codex worker's tool calls
                are capped"); --retries does not apply. Before the approval, Codex renders the launch's prompt
                offline and the launch is refused if it offers sub-agents (bin/_ext.py codex-probe).
  --wall-hours  wall-clock cap of the whole launch, every route (LESSONS.md 'A wall-clock cap on every route'): default 4 on the
                Claude routes, 2 on Codex. A Claude worker runs under `timeout` with one deadline across its
                rate-limit retries; at the cap it is stopped (TERM, KILL 60 s later) and EXIT-EXT says
                wall_cap_hit=1. No more hand-set systemd stop timers.
  --network     the worker gets the web: Claude routes get WebSearch, WebFetch and a Bash sandbox sharing the
                network; Codex gets live web search and a shared network. Brave/Exa go through a key-holding
                gateway outside the sandbox. Without --network a Codex worker reaches only the model provider,
                through an allowlisting egress proxy.
  --module NAME a licence module of the instance's kit-env.json (bin/_env.py): mounted for this worker, which on a run
                without the network reaches that module's licence servers and nothing else, through a relay here;
                every connection is logged (RUN/licence.log). Bound in the approval; checked before it is touched.
  --network and --via codex need RUN/HARNESS-NOTE.md for their route (bin/new-run --harness claude-net|codex|codex-net) and an
  approval that binds the flags (`-- <flags>`). Each leaves RUN/RECORD-EXT.md: hashes of the transcript, the
  gateway and egress logs and every file under RUN/downloads/, and the disclosure. --dry-run prints what
  would run and touches no approval.
  --detach      (user 2026-09-22 14:32) runs the launch as a systemd user service, kit-run-RUN, and
                returns once it has started; the run survives the calling shell and session. The approval is
                consumed inside the service as usual; --detach, like --dry-run, is never part of it. Output:
                .claude/state/ext/RUN/detached.out; exit status: detached.exit; watch: bin/watch-run RUN -f;
                stop: systemctl --user stop kit-run-RUN.
  bin/run-external --queue RUN1 RUN2 … [flags] [--detach]   (LESSONS.md 'A queue for runs approved together')
                runs approved together (bin/approve RUN1 RUN2 … -- flags), one at a time. Each run
                first passes this launcher's own checks (a dry run each); then every approval is used at once
                (bin/_approval.py queue: all checked, then all consumed, into a queue record the orchestrator cannot
                write), so no approval can expire while an earlier run works. Each run is released just before its
                launch (--queued NONCE, internal) only with the same flags and only if its bytes equal what was
                approved; a run whose bytes changed is refused and the queue goes on. QUEUE-START / QUEUE-RUN ledger
                lines. With --detach the whole queue runs as the user service kit-queue-<id>. The queue lives for
                the sum of its runs' wall caps plus 30 minutes. It stops after a run that ended on the plan's usage
                limit or the provider's capacity refusal (QUEUE-STOP); the runs not released need new approvals
                (LESSONS.md "A queue stops at the plan's usage limit").
  RUN    run name (e.g. 025-ext-canary) or path under workspace-*/runs/; BRIEF.md must exist.
  ID     via openrouter (the default): an OpenRouter model id, e.g. openai/gpt-6-astra or
         ~anthropic/claude-fable-latest; the key is read from $OPENROUTER_KEYFILE (default ~/.config/openrouter/key).
         via anthropic: the user's own Claude Code login (subscription), model alias or id such as
         fable, opus, sonnet, claude-fable-5-1. No OpenRouter key is read on this route.
         via codex: a Codex model id, e.g. gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-6-astra.
  --effort  checked here per route (Claude: low medium high xhigh max; Codex adds minimal), default high.
  --max-turns  default 300. A brief that allows more tool calls ("at most N tool calls") is refused here, before
               the approval is touched; bin/lint-brief warns of it first.

Limits (LESSONS.md "Limits are enforced, not promised"): the worker runs through bin/limits-exec, i.e. inside a systemd user scope
with CPUQuota = RD/.limits threads x 100 % and MemoryMax = mem_gb; the scope's cgroup CPU time of
the whole tree goes to RD/usage.json and the EXIT-EXT ledger line. Inside bwrap every command gets
ulimit -t (cpu_hours) and OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS = threads from the hook. The whole run's CPU budget
(RD/.limits cpu_hours) is enforced too: limits-exec stops the tree when it is spent, exit 152, cpu_cap_hit=1 on
EXIT-EXT (LESSONS.md "The whole-run CPU budget is enforced"). Without a systemd user manager nothing can be enforced,
so the launch is refused before the approval is touched (limits-exec --probe; P-3 B3).
The record: EXIT-EXT carries exit, wall time, attempts, the approved model, route and effort, effort_seen= (what
the requests carried), models_seen= and model_fallback= (the models that answered, from the transcript; LESSONS.md
"The model a worker ran on is recorded"), wall_cap_hit=, turn_cap_hit= (Codex: exit 125), plan_limit=,
at_capacity= and the usage figures. Every CLAUDE* and ANTHROPIC_* variable the parent session set or inherited
is dropped before launch (LESSONS.md "A parent session's routing never reaches a worker").
Sandbox: the worker process carries KIT_WORKER_RUN=<run dir>; .claude/hooks/sandbox.py applies
the kit-worker rules to any main process with that variable (binds it to the run dir, bwraps
Bash, denies everything else, ledgers every call). --setting-sources project,local keeps the
project hooks and drops user-scope hooks/settings; no-mcp.json drops user MCP servers.
No spending cap on any run (LESSONS.md 'No spending cap on any run', user 2026-09-25): --max-budget-usd is never
passed and --budget is refused; --max-turns is the turn cap. Logs: RUN/launch.log (stream-json; Codex: RUN/launch.jsonl), RUN/launch.err.
While the worker runs they are written to .claude/state/ext/RUN/logs/, which no worker can reach, and moved
into RUN at exit (user 2026-09-22 14:32: a worker must not be able to alter its own transcript).
RUN_EXTERNAL_DEBUG=1 adds Claude Code's API debug log (debug.log, same place).

Upstream rate limits (found in the source, 2026-09-16): OpenRouter answers a rate-limited Astra
request with an error object under HTTP 200, which Claude Code reports as "empty or malformed
response (HTTP 200)" and does not retry. When a run exits non-zero with that signature in the CLI's own words
(its stderr or its events, never a tool result or the model's text: P-12 H4), this
script waits (30 s, 60 s, 120 s, ...) and resumes the same session with `--resume` (or relaunches
fresh if the worker had not yet made a tool call), up to --retries times (default 3), ledgering
each RETRY-EXT.
```

## Lessons it cites

- → **Every worker is a headless main process**
- → **Every launch and every ledger append consumes a byte-bound**
- → **Networked and Codex launches need their flags bound**
- → **A Codex worker's tool calls are capped**
- → **A queue stops at the plan's usage limit**
- → **Limits are enforced, not promised**
- → **The whole-run CPU budget is enforced**
- → **The model a worker ran on is recorded**
- → **A parent session's routing never reaches a worker**
- → **A brief may not allow more tool calls than `--max-turns`**
- → **A run directory is launched once**
- → **No packet carries blocked material**
- → **A Codex worker has no sub-agents**
